tools.description: Start an execution (POST /v1/executions/{executionId}/start): a new executionId, mode, and file (a graph path on the Runtime host) or inline graph. held: true starts without driving. After a client timeout it may have started: read status, never retry. Mode governs proposals; pause holds dispatch.

held.description: true records the start without driving it (`execution start --held`), so it cannot outlast the client timeout.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

tools.name: start

tools.description: List executions (GET /v1/executions): one row per stream (id, mode, status, attention, head, start/last instants), by id. after: exclusive cursor; limit 1..=100 (default 20; larger refused). Read-only.

after.description: Exclusive cursor: the last execution id already read.

tools.name: list

tools.description: Read a graph file's shape (POST /v1/graph/topology): entrypoints, nodes, edges and the semantic hash. Match it to a run's execution_started graphHash before calling these edges that run's. file is on the Runtime host. Read-only.

file.description: Graph file path on the Runtime host.

tools.name: topology

tools.description: Read an execution's status (GET /v1/executions/{executionId}).
tools.name: status

tools.description: Read an execution's resume briefing (GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/briefing): purpose, executors, graph hash, decisions with their actors, work done, pending, next step. Call it FIRST when picking up a run another session drove. Read-only.
tools.name: briefing

tools.description: Read the proven-journey map (GET /v1/journeys, or GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/journeys for an existing run): each step's newest capture from any run, marked fresh, stale or unknown with the reason, and the walked arrows. Read-only.
tools.name: journeys

tools.description: Read a run's open task board (GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/tasks): each open task's step, lane, issue, PR, head, BLOCK, heartbeat. lane or issue narrows it (a few KB). Read-only.
tools.name: tasks

tools.description: Plan one task under keel.yaml (POST /v1/keel/plan; `graphhelm keel plan`): classifies its paths and returns the graphhelm-task-plan-v1 record (reviews, proof, skills, delegation, shortest path). judgeRoute lets Jev decide an ambiguous task. Read-only.
tools.name: keel_plan

tools.description: List the agent workspaces under the Runtime's --workspace-root (GET /v1/workspaces; `graphhelm workspace list`): lane, task, branch, state (claimed, released, swept), size on disk, and live git facts (head, dirty). Identical on CLI, HTTP and MCP. Read-only.
tools.name: workspace_list

tools.description: Remove released agent workspaces that are clean and still at the released commit (POST /v1/workspaces/sweep; `graphhelm workspace sweep --apply`). Never touches a path the ledger did not create and never follows a link. Owner sessions only: an agent-typed MCP session is refused.
tools.name: workspace_sweep

tools.description: List journey-flow sources (GET /v1/journey-flows; `graphhelm journey flows`): each flow's status, drift, validate findings, whether journey_approve would accept it, and its screens, edges and paths. Read-only.
tools.name: journey_flows

tools.description: Write a journey-flow draft through the Runtime (POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/draft). The Runtime records the authenticated scoped agent as writer; unscoped and owner-only credentials are refused.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

tools.name: journey_draft

tools.description: Review a journey-flow draft through the Runtime (POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/review). The Runtime requires a different scoped agent from every writer of the current digest.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

tools.name: journey_review

tools.description: Approve one journey flow (POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/approve; `graphhelm journey approve`): binds it to HEAD, clears drift and writes its contracts. Refused, writing nothing, while validate reports findings. Owner sessions only.
tools.name: journey_approve

tools.description: Open an approved journey live at one step (POST /v1/journeys/{contractId}/open): a visible browser replays the earlier edges' cached acts and reports the step's state. The reply's sessionId addresses journey_act and journey_close. Owner credential only.
tools.name: journey_open

tools.description: Send one act to an open live journey session (POST /v1/journeys/sessions/{sessionId}/act; exactly `graphhelm journey act`) and report the screen it lands on and that screen's state. Destructive-looking names are refused unless the approved flow has that act. Owner credential only.
tools.name: journey_act

tools.description: Play a journey flow paced for a person (POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/watch): headless with frames in the Studio, or window: true. Optional path, paceMs. Answers when play ends; journey_sessions shows it meanwhile. Never proof or approval. Owner only.
tools.name: journey_watch

tools.description: Run a journey flow headless on every path, keeping per screen and edge whether it passed (POST /v1/journey-flows/{id}/preview). Answers the kept result or starts a run; force reruns; read: true only reads (GET /v1/journey-flows/{id}/preview). Never proof. Owner only.
tools.name: journey_preview

tools.description: Close an open live journey session and its browser (DELETE /v1/journeys/sessions/{sessionId}; exactly `graphhelm journey close`). Owner credential only.
tools.name: journey_close

tools.description: List the Runtime project's open live journey sessions (GET /v1/journeys/sessions; exactly `graphhelm journey sessions`): each session's contract, step, state (pass, fail, drift, unknown), code, the screen it is on and when it last acted. Read-only. Owner credential only.
tools.name: journey_sessions

tools.description: Read an execution's event tail (GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/events with after/limit passed straight through; the API's bounds are the bounds).
tools.name: events

tools.description: Open the content behind an evidence reference (GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/evidence/{evidenceId}); for up to eight references in one execution, use GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/evidence?ids=<JSON array>.
tools.name: evidence

lane.description: Lane to sign as; with credentialFile.

tools.description: Arm THIS session's wake lease (POST /v1/executions/{executionId}/wake-lease): one content-free ring when the log moves past the cursor. A session can only ever arm itself; no tool rings another session.

cursor.description: Ring for appends AFTER this sequence; defaults to the head.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

maturesInSeconds.description: Quiet allowed before the wait ends by itself; omitted, only an append rings.

rendezvousId.description: Opaque rendezvous identity — never a filesystem path; the sidecar derives the platform rendezvous from it.

tools.name: wake_arm

tools.description: Read THIS session's live wake lease (GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/wake-lease).
tools.name: wake_status

tools.description: Declare how long one node may stay silent before it needs you (POST /v1/executions/{executionId}/amend-budget), from now on. It is the remedy status names for a node it reads as unknown. Replies with the recomputed verdict.

computedAtSequence.description: The frontier the verdict you are answering was computed at. A stale amendment is refused with the current one.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

seconds.description: The bound YOU decide. Nothing here suggests one.

tools.name: amend_budget

tools.description: Block until this session's armed wake lease rings or its deadline passes, both read from GET /v1/executions/{executionId}/wake-lease: pass an identity, never a duration. The block is local and is NOT an API call. The reply says that something happened, never what.
tools.name: wake_wait

tools.description: Add or replace one direct_api route in the gateway manifest (PUT /v1/gateway/routes). Declaration only: the API key is never an argument, since it would land in the transcript; key the route with `gateway credential set` or the HTTP body.

baseUrl.description: https://..., or http:// to a loopback address. No trailing slash.

contextWindowTokens.description: Input context window in tokens (ADR-042). Absent on a replace: kept; 0 clears.

credentialRef.description: The broker reference holding this route's key. Absent: secret_<id>.

enabled.description: Absent: true. False parks the route: listed, and refused at dispatch.

id.description: The route id callers name. Unique in the manifest: an existing id needs replace.

manifest.description: Manifest path override; absent, the Runtime's own.

provider.description: The wire format, not the vendor: a DeepSeek endpoint is openai with its own baseUrl.

replace.description: Absent: false, and an existing id is refused with the manifest left byte-identical.

tiers.description: Delegation tiers served (ADR-041). Absent on a replace: kept; [] clears.

tools.name: route_set

Requires content, exact workspace/project, expiry, sourceExecutionId and a separately authenticated validatorSignalId. ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

tools.name: sweep

tools.description: Claim a waiting_input node's external work is done (POST /v1/executions/{executionId}/claim). Testimony only: nothing releases until clear countersigns. Graph optional; waitSeq and asserter default.

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

tools.name: claim

tools.description: Countersign a claim by machine replay (POST /v1/executions/{executionId}/clear) with manifestHash or the evidence bundle: a match clears the node and drives dependents, a mismatch is journaled. Graph optional; claimSeq defaults to the open claim. countersign is refused (#529).

ifMatch.description: Optional If-Match head pin: 409 if the store moved past it.

tools.name: clear

tools.description: Compile a goal into a graph document (POST /v1/graphs/synthesize): one model draft, validated like an authored file, repaired at most twice, or refused with diagnostics. Starts nothing: pass it to start as graph. allowPrograms never widens; fixture is a replies file on the Runtime host.

allowPrograms.description: Programs a shell node may name; defaults to the server's own allowlist and is never widened by the compiler.

critic.description: design adds a design step and a blind critic before the draft.

drafts.description: How many drafts to ask for and rank; more than one needs a judge.

execution.description: The run this graph is built for; without critic and plan, the run's newest trusted keel.plan record decides.

fixture.description: Recorded-replies file path on the Runtime host: the keyless model door.

goal.description: What the graph must achieve, in the operator's words.

judgeFixture.description: Recorded-answers file path on the Runtime host: the keyless judge door.

judgeRoute.description: A direct_api typesafe route id for the judge. Exclusive with judgeFixture; no judge, no judgment.

library.description: A template directory path on the Runtime host the judge may choose to reuse or adapt.

plan.description: keel_plan's graphhelm-task-plan-v1 record; its critic applies when critic is absent.

route.description: A route id of the server's manifest; the deployer's default when absent.

tools.name: synthesize

tools.description: Assign a node to a responsible actor (POST /v1/executions/{executionId}/assign). Owner-only: the Runtime refuses any other actor type, so an agent session cannot assign work to itself. The recorded event keeps the assigned actor separate from the owner who recorded it.
